parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A charged sphere $X$ is supported on an insulating stand. A second charged sphere $Y$ is suspended by an insulating thread so that sphere $Y$ is in equilibrium at the position shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:figure_4_1.png}}

The charge on sphere $X$ is $+96\text{ nC}$ and the charge on sphere $Y$ is $+64\text{ nC}$.

Assume that the spheres behave as point charges.

The length of the thread is $1.2\text{ m}$ and the centres of sphere $X$ and sphere $Y$ are separated horizontally by a distance of $0.080\text{ m}$.
parts.text:
On Fig. 4.2, draw and label all the forces acting on sphere $Y$.

{{figure:figure_4_2.png}}

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Calculate the total electric potential energy stored between X and Y.

$$\text{energy} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{J}$$

(J)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
An electron enters the region between two parallel plates $P$ and $Q$, that are separated by a distance of $18\text{ mm}$, as shown in Fig. 4.3.

{{figure:figure_4_3.png}}

The space between the plates is a vacuum.

The potential difference between the plates is $250\text{ V}$. The electric field may be assumed to be uniform in the region between the plates and zero outside this region.
parts.text: State the direction of the electric force on the electron when between the plates.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Determine the magnitude of the force acting on the electron due to the electric field.

$$\text{force} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{N}$$

(N)

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the electron does not follow a circular path.
